All three reviewer findings were valid and are fixed in the figure briefs only; no application text needed to change.

**Fixes applied**

- **FIG-3 / FIG-6, cam ring drive face (critical):** removed the assertion that the drive face sits adjacent to the right segment junction. The disclosure says only that the wedge is driven against a drive face of the cam ring, and separately that complementary end faces couple the segments; it never locates the face circumferentially. Both briefs now place the face on the ring band clear of both junctions, which shows the disclosed function without asserting that latch drive enters the ring at a segment end.
- **FIG-1 / FIG-2, mounting boss (minor):** dropped "projects radially outward from the outer boundary." The source locates the boss only "outside the annular guide," which does not choose between a radial projection beyond the periphery and a boss on an axial face. Both briefs now show it schematically on the frame; FIG-2 keeps the source-grounded relation "outside the annular guide that holds the cam ring." The clear-of-hinge-and-latch legibility constraint in FIG-1 remains.
- **FIG-2 / FIG-5, part designations (minor):** "slideway" is now "radial guide" and "channel" is now "annular guide" throughout, matching draft/numerals.md, the detailed description, the claims and draft/07-drawings.md, so numerals 24 and 36 are named identically in every view.

Numerals, figure count, and numeral-per-sheet limits are unchanged; the briefs range 1337 to 2063 characters, all within limit, and a scan of draft/ and figures/ finds no placeholder, drafting note, or em dash. input.summary: Resolved all three findings from the previous QA report by correcting figure briefs only; no change was needed to any draft/ section, because the specification and claims were already neutral on both contested geometry points. (1) Critical: FIG-3 and FIG-6 had fixed the circumferential position of the cam ring drive face (54) "adjacent to the right junction." The disclosure states only that closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring; it never locates that face on the ring, and locating it at a segment end would assert that latch drive enters one segment and reaches the other only through the coupling faces. Both briefs now place the drive face on the ring band clear of the slots and clear of both junctions. (2) Minor: FIG-1 and FIG-2 had the mounting boss (66) projecting radially outward from the frame outer boundary; the source says only "outside the annular guide," which does not distinguish a radial projection beyond the periphery from a boss on an axial face. Both briefs now show the boss schematically on the frame, FIG-2 retaining the source-grounded relation "outside the annular guide that holds the cam ring," with the legibility-only clear-of-hinge-and-latch requirement kept in FIG-1. (3) Minor: numeral 24 was called a "slideway" and numeral 36 a "channel" in FIG-2 and FIG-5, while the numeral table, description and claims call them "radial guide" and "annular guide"; the briefs now use the canonical designations everywhere. Numeral placement targets for 24, 36, 54 and 66 were updated in step. No numeral was added, removed, or reassigned, the six-figure set is unchanged, every brief remains well under 2800 characters, and a scan of draft/ and figures/ shows no placeholder, drafting note, or em dash. I edit specifications only: FIGS. 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 need re-rendering from the corrected briefs, and the pixel-level visual, OCR and leader gates cannot be confirmed by me.
reasoning: The critical finding was correct on the substance, not merely on style. A drive face is a functional load-transfer surface, so saying where it sits circumferentially is an assertion about how force enters the segmented ring. Placing it immediately beside a junction implies the wedge loads the very end of one segment and that the second segment is driven only through the complementary end faces. The disclosure supports neither proposition, so the position had to come out rather than be softened with schematic hedging.

I fixed the drive face in the figure briefs alone because draft/08-detailed-description.md and draft/09-claims.md recite only 'a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30' with no position. Widening or narrowing the text to match a drawing would have inverted the correct authority order, in which the sources govern the text and the text governs the sheets.

For the mounting boss, the neutral phrasing was the conservative option that keeps the disclosed non-participating nature intact. 'Outside the annular guide' is a relation to the guide, not to the frame periphery, so FIG-2 keeps that exact relation while FIG-1, which does not show the annular guide, now says only that the boss is on the frame. I kept the clear-of-hinge-and-latch instruction in FIG-1 because it separates the boss from two other numbered parts in the same view and is legibility, not invention geometry.

The designation mismatch was worth fixing even though the reviewer conceded the referents were unambiguous. A single part named two ways across views invites an examiner objection under the drawing-consistency practice and weakens antecedent basis arguments later, and the cost of conforming the briefs to the numeral table was nil since the draft text already used the canonical terms.

I deliberately left the rest of the draft alone. The source-fidelity gate reported as failing was driven entirely by the three listed items, and the reviewer had already traced every limitation of all 17 claims and all 28 numerals as clean, so reopening the claims or background would have destroyed verified work to no benefit.

I did not treat the review report itself as disclosure authority. Its recitation of technical detail, including its summary of the claim limitations and its suggested figure wording, names details in order to audit or reject them, which is not affirmative source support. Each replacement wording was checked back against the disclosure passage on the mounting boss and the drive face before being written.

No rendered artifact was touched, and no numeral, claim, description or numeral-table text changed — the numeral sets on every sheet are unchanged, so the table, drawing descriptions, detailed description and claims stay in sync as they were.

On FIG. 6 I made the brief unambiguous in the direction the disclosure already requires: the cam ring is segmented into exactly two arcuate segments meeting at two junctions, and there are exactly three oblique slots, one per jaw carriage. The short ring drive face is now explicitly a face on the outer edge rather than an opening, which is what the image model appears to have miscounted as a fourth slot.

One note carried over from the drafting brief: no prior-art search was run and no `prior_art/` material was supplied with this repair, so the art considered may be incomplete. This repair is corrective QA only and adds no new subject matter.

structured_output.summary: All six gate failures are drawing-side and are repaired in the authoritative figure briefs only; no rendered artifact was edited, and the claims, detailed description, numeral table, and drawing descriptions are unchanged because no repair required a change to them. FIG-1, FIG-2 and FIG-5 failed OCR because the caption rendered as a loose "FIG" plus a detached figure digit (and, on FIG-1, because the numeral 10 split into two digits); each brief now requires the caption to render as one continuous label with a tight period and a single ordinary word space, and requires each multi-digit numeral to render as one tight digit group with no gap, leader, or drawing line passing between its digits. FIG-3 failed a semantic review that read the brief's prohibition sentences as banning all text; its sheet text section, and those of all six briefs, now state affirmatively that one caption and the listed numerals are required and scope the prohibition to everything else. FIG-4's failure was an HTTP read timeout against the OCR service rather than a defect in the sheet; its brief receives the same caption and numeral hardening so the forced re-render is re-inspected under the tightened spec. FIG-6 failed on perspective and on a fourth slot: the view paragraph now forbids tilt, vanishing point, offset duplicate circles, side walls, rim faces and any depth line, and requires both ring boundaries to be true circles of equal width and height; the fourth opening was the unnumbered drive face carried over from FIG. 3, which is now removed from that sheet, with the opening count stated as an absolute total of three and junction breaks stated not to count as slots. Removing the drive face from FIG. 6 needs no text patch, since FIG. 6 numbers only the junction drive faces 44, 46, 48 and 50, and the description and drawing list cite ring drive face 54 to FIGS. 3 and 4 only. Separately, as the drafting brief directs: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art on hand may be incomplete.
changes: FIG-1 brief: sheet text section rebuilt. Caption must render as one continuous label (tight period, single ordinary word space before the figure number, nothing between letters and number, no leader or drawing line through or near it); added a rule that each reference numeral renders as one tight digit group so 10 cannot split into 1 and 0; prohibition reworded to scope it to text other than the required caption and numerals.
FIG-2 brief: same sheet text rebuild, keyed to the caption FIG. 2, addressing the unexpected digit 2, the stray FIG token and the wrong figure label.

FIG-3 brief: sheet text section rebuilt to state affirmatively that one caption and the listed reference numerals are required text on the sheet, with the no-other-lettering prohibition scoped to everything else, clearing the semantic review finding that the sheet was required to carry no text or digits.

FIG-4 brief: same sheet text rebuild, keyed to the caption FIG. 4, forcing a fresh render and a fresh OCR pass after the transient vision service read timeout, and inspecting it under the tightened caption and numeral rules.
FIG-5 brief: same sheet text rebuild, keyed to the caption FIG. 5, addressing the unexpected digit 5, the stray FIG token and the wrong figure label.

FIG-6 brief: view paragraph rewritten to force a strictly two dimensional plane figure. Line of sight exactly along the ring axis and perpendicular to the page; no tilt of any amount, no vanishing point, horizon, ground plane or shadow; outer and inner boundaries are true circles of equal width and height sharing one center; no offset duplicate circle, side wall, rim face, edge highlight or any other depth line, so the ring has no thickness.

FIG-6 brief: slot bullet rewritten so three is stated as the absolute total count of openings through the band, with no fourth slot, partial slot, hole, notch, aperture or elongated closed outline anywhere in the view, and the unnumbered drive face carried over from FIG. 3 removed from this sheet so nothing can be read as a fourth slot.
FIG-6 brief: junction bullet clarified that a junction is a break in the band rather than an enclosed opening within it, and is not counted as a slot.
